svg.title: Allocate Startup Cash Before Adding Fixed Rent
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate Startup Cash Before Adding Fixed Rent; subtitle: Four buckets reconcile $12,000 lean, $30,000 planning, and $60,000 upper budgets.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative allocations within the canonical $12,000–$60,000 startup range. Numeric values encode the $30,000 planning stack; each stage also supplies lean and upper allocations. Weights remain 30%, 35%, 20%, and 15%. These are cash uses, not four immediate profit-and-loss expenses.; caption: Lean totals $12,000; planning totals $30,000; upper totals $60,000. Validate deposits and furnishing quotes before choosing a property count.; stages: label: Lease-entry cash; value: $3,600 lean; $9,000 planning; $18,000 upper allocation; numeric value: 9000.0; detail: Thirty percent funds landlord security deposits and contractually required prepaid rent. Track refundable deposits as assets and prepaid rent by service period; neither is automatically an immediate operating expense.; label: Furniture and property setup; value: $4,200 lean; $10,500 planning; $21,000 upper allocation; numeric value: 10500.0; detail: Thirty-five percent funds furniture, linens, kitchen equipment, installation, and initial readiness work. Obtain property-specific quotes; distinguish durable assets from consumables and avoid assuming one budget equips an arbitrary number of units.; label: Vacancy and collection liquidity; value: $2,400 lean; $6,000 planning; $12,000 upper allocation; numeric value: 6000.0; detail: Twenty percent remains available for vacancy gaps, payer delays, and early-closeout rent exposure. This cash reserve is not a deductible expense merely because it has been assigned to a budget bucket.; label: Launch systems and risk setup; value: $1,800 lean; $4,500 planning; $9,000 upper allocation; numeric value: 4500.0; detail: Fifteen percent funds insurance inception payments, contract preparation, access equipment, bookkeeping setup, and workflow configuration. Separate recurring charges from prepayments and installed assets.

rect.title: label: Lease-entry cash; numeric value: 9000.0; value: $3,600 lean; $9,000 planning; $18,000 upper allocation; detail: Thirty percent funds landlord security deposits and contractually required prepaid rent. Track refundable deposits as assets and prepaid rent by service period; neither is automatically an immediate operating expense.

This cash reserve is not a deductible expense merely because it has been assigned to a budget bucket.
